entries.test: ppr-shell.test.ts > ppr-shell caching (dev) > a cold partial request captures a PPR snapshot for a later prefetch
entries.reason: #1079, rule 2, the timing gap on a slot: a parallel slot's loader boundary reads the loader aggregate itself (slots get no per-loader streams, src/segment-system.tsx:833-884; LoaderResolver's use(loaderDataPromise), src/route-content-wrapper.tsx:334). getMemoizedLoaderPromise hands the aggregate as a promise when the tree is built while it is pending (src/segment-loader-promise.ts:134); when it settles before React renders the slot, React suspends on a settled promise and the @badge slot mounts its loading() fallback. Seen once in a full dev run at load 20-49; 0 of 6 reruns, and 0 of 6 with 8x CPU throttling. Timing-dependent.

entries.test: navigation.test.ts > stale-revalidation > should update quantity on intercept after action on detail page and back navigation
entries.reason: Undeclared, cause: an action started on the intercepted /product/product-a completes after a navigation to the same URL without the intercept (View full details). The action bridge reconciles the response's matched ids, computed for the intercept page (the home route M0L0L0R0 and its ProductsLoader under the modal), against the detail page's cache (src/browser/server-action-bridge.ts:709, segment-reconciler.ts:184) before classifyActionOutcome (server-action-bridge.ts:726) sees the history key change and discards the result; pathname checks cannot tell the two pages apart. Reproduced on origin/main.

entries.test: progressive-enhancement.test.ts > progressive-enhancement > with JavaScript enabled > form submission should work with JS enhancement
entries.reason: Undeclared, cause: the fixture's form passes method="post" next to a server function action (e2e/test-app/src/urls/hooks.handlers.tsx:390). React's server renderer writes the server reference's method (POST) and the client compares the prop (post); React also logs that method is overridden for a function action. A fixture issue, not the router. Reproduced on origin/main.
